title: Chronic kidney disease: stage, hypertension and dialysis status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's kidney disease and any related hypertension and dialysis status.
note:
Chief Complaint
Fatigue and decreased urine output.

HPI
The patient presents today reporting increased fatigue over the last two weeks. He notes that his urine output has been slightly lower than usual. He has a history significant for hypertension and chronic kidney disease, currently classified as stage 2. He reports adherence to his current medication regimen. He denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or leg swelling.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10 mg daily
Furosemide 20 mg daily

Exam
Vitals are stable. Cardiovascular exam is unremarkable. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Abdomen is soft and non-tender. Physical exam reveals no peripheral edema.

Assessment
The patient has stage 2 kidney disease and managed hypertension. Current symptoms appear stable.

Plan
Continue current medications. Monitor dietary sodium intake closely to help manage hypertension. Follow up in three months or sooner if symptoms worsen.
explanations: Hypertension with CKD is presumed linked: I12.9 for CKD stage 1-4 (sequenced first), plus the N18 stage code.

distractors.why: The classification presumes a link between hypertension and CKD.
I12.0 is for stage 5 or ESRD only.
